claims: state agreements pay well above the floor, in some cases by more than $25,000 a year at the entry step
whys: Hard-coded dollar figure in prose. It will go stale when either the award or a state scale changes, and it is not derived from the RN_ENTRY or AWARD_RN1 data rendered elsewhere on the page.

claims: The Nurses Award 2020 is the single most searched-for nursing pay document in Australia ... It sets the minimum below which no nurse in the country may lawfully be paid.
whys: 'Single most searched-for' has no cited source. 'No nurse in the country' overreaches: the modern award covers national-system employers, and state public sector nurses in the state industrial systems (NSW, Qld, WA, SA, Tas) are covered by state instruments, not the federal award.

claims: Under the award, ordinary hours on a Saturday pay 150% and on a Sunday 175%; a weekday afternoon shift attracts 12.5% and a weekday night shift 15%.
whys: Award penalty percentages are hard-coded in prose and in the penalty table row (line 344) rather than read from award data, so they will not update with the award.

claims: Night shift is worth 20% in NSW, 20% in Queensland, 20.5% in South Australia, a flat dollar allowance per shift in Victoria and 35% in Western Australia ... wrong in at least four states.
whys: These state night-shift percentages are typed into the prose and again into the penalty table cells at lines 336-342, instead of being read from each state's nursing-pay data. The 'at least four states' count is also hand-computed. Both will go stale when any state agreement changes.

claims: Where more than one penalty could apply to the same hours, only the highest is paid.
whys: lib/constants/hospitality-award.ts line 154 records an exception (highestOnlyException): the clause 16 breaks penalty is paid in addition to the highest penalty (cl 29.3(c)). The FAQ states the rule with no exception.
reviewerNotes: The writer's question is valid. 'Only the highest is paid' leaves out HOSPITALITY_PENALTIES.highestOnlyException (cl 29.3(c), the breaks penalty paid in addition), recorded at lib/constants/hospitality-award.ts:154.

claims: General Retail Industry Award casual overtime is pct(1.75) against pct(1.5) for permanents.
whys: The retail overtime multipliers are hard-coded literals in the template, not read from RETAIL_PENALTIES or a retail overtime constant, so they will not update with the data.
The 80% is typed into the prose, not read from the retail junior scale constant. The source comment at hospitality-award.ts:167 agrees with it, but it should come from data.
